name: Buru
catalog_quote: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. Stress is not affected by the addition of suffixes or enclitics, such as the phrase-level plural marker /-ro/, or by the addition of paragogic /e/.. (Grimes 1995)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict penultimate, word domain' is supported by the best available source, which we hold: Grimes 1991 p.52 sec. 5.2.1 (penultimate syllable of full lexical roots; affixes do not affect it because suffixal enclitics -k/-t/-n/-h are non-syllabic; plural -ro and paragogic /e/ are explicitly extrametrical, giving surface antepenultimate fúka-ro), p.54 sec. 5.2.3 (the one syllabic suffix -i shifts stress to the new penult, i.e. stress tracks the penult of root+suffix), p.55 (stress never final), p.59 (rare trisyllabic roots eC-CV́-CV also penultimate), p.53 (cliticised roots/proclitics unstressed; phrase stress on last stressed syllable). No lexical exceptions or loan-stress irregularities are reported in the sections read.
